text: One private detail can reach a whole audience in one frame. It can spread from the screen to chat, then into clips. Veil gives the streamer a way to respond.
Here is a slow replay of real OBS output. Veil checks the screen on this computer. Solid masks cover the private text it finds. Late checks keep the frame covered.
If a check is late, Paranoid covers the frame. It also covers frames that have no result. Slow checks can keep the screen covered. The app shows this limit.
I add a fake private address to Never Show. Veil encrypts it on this computer. A PIN controls reveal. Sharing a term with Twitch is a separate choice.
Veil connects to Twitch and OBS. The connection is real. Preflight checks the scene, audio timing, chat connection, and delay budget. A green connection badge alone is not enough.
I press Panic. OBS changes to the cover scene. Veil opens an incident and records each action. It asks before optional actions run. No is the default.
The private chat guard checks altered words and repeated attempts. It keeps private terms on this computer. The action log shows what succeeded, what failed, and what needs review.
The report lists times and actions. It leaves private text out by default. Clips are listed for human review. Veil restores the original audio offsets when it closes.
The screen check, private words, and incident record stay local. Twitch handles the enabled account actions. Codex helped build the system. GitHub Actions checks the code and platform packages.
We built this in one main Codex chat. Both text matchers use the same test cases. A three thousand image benchmark checks detection. Native OBS tests check the rendered masks.
Veil helps streamers prevent a leak, contain the response, and review the incident. Private boundaries. Clear control.
